correctness.rationale: The established one-dimensional spectral bands have equal masses and exact p-step returns, with the stated open-lower/closed-upper slope convention. Independence is preserved by the shift and the single coordinate update. The map then advances the product cells by the displayed affine permutation and F^(dp) is exactly the product of the p-step one-dimensional returns. Exactness follows by tensoring on rectangular simple functions and extending by L¹ contraction; a map with an exact positive power is exact. Thus a least cycle of length ℓ is one ergodic component under the natural product probability and gives precisely ℓ mutually singular phase limits in the stated a.c. sense. In a k-step shift the index permutation splits into g=gcd(d,k) cycles; summing carry increments along each index cycle gives k/g. There is one free base label per cycle exactly when p divides that carry. Burnside and divisor inversion give the formulas. The proof's phrase ‘group generated by R, of order dp’ should instead say the action of Z/(dp) by powers of R: for p=1 the permutation is the identity on a singleton, but the formula uses the valid nonfaithful action and still returns one component of period 1. The independent replay confirms the two histograms, the singleton, and the four rational cyclic intervals at β=11/10, and checks the fixed-count formula against 30 integer-encoded orbit histograms.
residual_risks: Scope is zero coupling and densities a.c. with respect to the natural product invariant measure. No result for other invariant measures, off-core points, or small nonzero coupling is inferred.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Topological transitivity alone is not a measure-theoretic proof, but the older exact band returns supply the stronger measure property on the symmetric tent core, without need for a new spectral computation. The synchronous coupled-map article is related but is not the decisive overlap.

evidence: In Simpson's notation k=p and n=d, a power i not divisible by p has no fixed labels; for i=jp the count is p^g when g=gcd(i,d) divides j, and zero otherwise. This is exactly p|i/g. A positive-power return on any cell here is the direct product of the known p-step returns.
§12 expressly says each trapping region of g contains a unique attractor and asks whether that generalizes to nearby f; it does not claim the product-ACIP spectral theorem verbatim.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Divisor inversion of the published fixed-point data gives the histogram immediately. Because finite products of exact probability maps are exact, the established exact returns make those same orbit unions the ergodic components with no hidden splitting. The algebraic count and its straightforward exact-return interpretation do not leave a distinct scientific result as framed.

originality.rationale: Simpson's 2022 paper already treats the same cyclic-product phase permutation, derives equivalent fixed-power counts and the orbit count, and explicitly gives the one-four/five-twelve example. The period histogram is obtained from those counts by divisor inversion. Simpson also explicitly argues that each region has one attractor in the unperturbed skew product, by local eventual onto and transitivity; his open question concerns perturbations, not the unperturbed product. The frozen measure-theoretic formulation is not quoted as stated in Simpson, but on the given exact bands it follows directly from the published partition and a textbook finite product of exact returns, since F^(dp) acts coordinatewise. Thus the central census and its claimed novelty are covered, and the remaining a.c. interpretation is a direct consequence of the already established structure, not a disproof of the mathematical finding.
residual_risks: Losson–Mackey 1995 full text was inaccessible; this does not drive the verdict. No general priority verdict about measure-theoretic terminology or nonzero coupling is made.

value.rationale: Separating visible boxes from statistical components is a useful interpretation. Here the natural census, nontrivial example, and unperturbed no-splitting structure are already supplied by the previous box-orbit analysis and one-dimensional band decomposition. The remaining statistical formulation follows mechanically by tensoring the established exact returns and applying the standard orbit inversion; it gives no distinct unresolved target worth retaining as an independent finding. It could serve as an expository correction to avoid reading a sixteen-patch plot as a proof of a sixteen-phase ergodic component.
residual_risks: This judgment does not apply to proving persistence under coupling, a different invariant measure, or a separate result requiring new spectral or mixing estimates.
